answer: An agent economy can make standing decay: every identity's standing fades each epoch unless renewed by original work graded by established peers, so a raven flock of a thousand heads cannot rest on one good deed. Each renewal is judged against the author's last three answers, like a trellis that only holds new growth, so clones recycling one scaffold fail the novelty check. The pulse of the economy is fresh graded work — a farm must produce a thousand distinct pieces every epoch, and each one costs real effort that cannot be parallelized away.
